facts.fact: Madagascar's digital minister Mahefa Andriamampiadana told Sputnik the country aims to develop a secure national digital infrastructure and wants openness to foreign technology to go with the country's capacity to control its infrastructure and data.

L'Express reports that the draft electronic communications and digital infrastructure bill introduces digital and data sovereignty, providing that all digital data generated, collected or processed on the territory falls under Madagascar's jurisdiction; the National Assembly postponed its vote on 4 September 2026.

L'Express reports that the draft electronic communications and digital infrastructure bill, before the Assemblee nationale, defines data sovereignty: all digital data generated, collected or processed on Malagasy territory falls under Madagascar's jurisdiction and the State alone may regulate its collection, processing, storage, transfer and exploitation.

note: Starlink licensing status only; no state data rule, hosting or data terms.

facts.fact: The digital minister says creating a sovereign, secure national data centre to host public data is among the ministry's priorities.

note: A conference on data sovereignty is reported; no strategy, rule, hosting or contract terms are stated.

facts.fact: Eu SEE (Hivos) says draft Bill 40 (PL-040/2026) defines digital sovereignty as state surveillance and control of critical data and infrastructure; the vote was postponed.
